description: The U.S. calendar lists this date as a weekday in Ordinary Time.
catholic_connection: Green marks Ordinary Time and points to growth in the Christian life through prayer, repentance, work, and charity.

title: Friday of the Thirty-First Week in Ordinary Time
summary: Ordinary Time continues in the Thirty-First Week.
description: The U.S. calendar lists this date as a weekday in Ordinary Time.
catholic_connection: Green marks Ordinary Time and points to growth in the Christian life through prayer, repentance, work, and charity.

title: Saturday of the Thirty-First Week in Ordinary Time
summary: The Church keeps a Saturday weekday in Ordinary Time.
description: The U.S. calendar lists this as a weekday and indicates that the Blessed Virgin Mary may be observed on Saturday.
catholic_connection: Saturday observances of the Blessed Virgin Mary are optional and should not be treated as replacing the weekday unless chosen in the liturgy.

title: Thirty-Second Sunday in Ordinary Time
summary: The Church gathers for the Thirty-Second Sunday in Ordinary Time.
description: The U.S. calendar lists this date as the Thirty-Second Sunday in Ordinary Time.
catholic_connection: Sunday is the Lord's Day, the weekly celebration of Christ's Resurrection in the life of the Church.

title: The Dedication of the Lateran Basilica
summary: The Church celebrates the Dedication of the Lateran Basilica, cathedral church of the Bishop of Rome.
description: The U.S. calendar keeps the Dedication of the Lateran Basilica as a feast.
catholic_connection: This feast points to the Church as a visible communion gathered for worship, not merely to a building.

title: Saint Leo the Great, Pope and Doctor of the Church
summary: The Church honors Saint Leo the Great, pope and Doctor of the Church.
description: The U.S. calendar keeps Saint Leo the Great as a memorial.
catholic_connection: White is used for saints who were not martyrs. Leo's memorial points to teaching, pastoral authority, and defense of the faith.

title: Saint Martin of Tours, Bishop
summary: The Church honors Saint Martin of Tours, bishop and pastor.
description: The U.S. calendar keeps Saint Martin of Tours as a memorial.
catholic_connection: White is used for saints who were not martyrs. Martin's memorial points to charity, pastoral care, and holiness in public witness.

title: Saint Josaphat, Bishop and Martyr
summary: The Church honors Saint Josaphat, bishop and martyr.
description: The U.S. calendar keeps Saint Josaphat as a memorial.
catholic_connection: Red is used for martyrs. His memorial points to fidelity to Christ and love for the unity of the Church.

title: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, Virgin
summary: In the United States, the Church honors Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, virgin and missionary.
description: The U.S. calendar keeps Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, Virgin, as a memorial in the United States.
catholic_connection: White is used for saints who were not martyrs. Cabrini's memorial points to missionary charity and care for immigrants.

title: Saturday of the Thirty-Second Week in Ordinary Time
summary: The Church keeps a Saturday weekday in Ordinary Time.
description: The U.S. calendar lists this as a weekday and indicates that the Blessed Virgin Mary may be observed on Saturday.
catholic_connection: Saturday observances of the Blessed Virgin Mary are optional and should not be treated as replacing the weekday unless chosen in the liturgy.

title: Thirty-Third Sunday in Ordinary Time
summary: The Church gathers for the Thirty-Third Sunday in Ordinary Time.
description: The U.S. calendar lists this date as the Thirty-Third Sunday in Ordinary Time. Saint Albert the Great is not the primary general-calendar entry this year because the date falls on Sunday.
catholic_connection: Sunday is the Lord's Day and takes precedence over ordinary memorials in the Roman calendar.
